Our Values & Ethos
In anything we do for the pupils we must be thoroughly prepared, totally committed and hugely enthusiastic because we never want to think afterwards “What a wasted opportunity”. We are a first choice school for parents within Lewisham local authority, for children and young people identified with specific needs. Our desire to get better, ability to try new things and learn from our errors, our blatant refusal to stand still and our commitment to make it happen must be at the heart of everything we do.
We aim to help each student by:
To support this aim we:
To be the most effective and innovative mixed provision for pupils with SEMH in key stages 1-4
We aim for every pupil to achieve his or her full potential. Every student will leave New Woodlands literate, numerate and with the functional communication and self regulation skills to participate in society including education, training and employment.
Developing their talents and aspirations
Provide a safe and supportive learning environment
Offer a relevant curriculum with differentiated work
Promote self-esteem
Celebrate success

pageCache.text:
Welcome
We are a special school who support all children from 5 to 16 who have SEMH as their main need. We admit children from all Lewisham mainstream schools who are referred to us. We will support the child and the family to put in support mechanisms and strategies to help manage behaviour/learning progress.
We have an open door policy for all parents and encourage you to come up to the school no matter how small your worry may be, we can nearly always find a solution to the problem.
We recognise the most difficult job in the world is bringing up children in modern society and are here to help support all parents and carers through what is often a difficult time in that child/young person’s life.

Our Governors
Our Governing Body is led by a very experienced and well established Chair of governors.
The Governing Body includes:
Parent governors are elected to serve on the governing body by the parents and normally serve for four years.
Our staff governor is elected by the staff of the school and also normally serves for four years.
Co-opted governors are invited onto the governing body, by the other governors, to add areas of expertise and to represent a cross section of the local community.
The governing body is responsible for many important decisions in the running of the school. These include:
Pen Portraits of Governors
Devon Elliott I am born, raised and educated in south London having attend Greenwich university for all my under and post graduate education. I am married with 2 young boys. I am currently the head of evidence and evaluation for community health services in NHS England and have worked in the NHS for 17 years both clinically in a nursing role for Adults and Children with learning disabilities with challenging behaviour and in various non – clinical roles. I led on safeguarding adults reporting for mental health services in Lambeth for almost a decade, I was the lead analyst for adult mental health in South London and Maudsley (SLaM) across Croydon, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark focused on the AMH transformation to move towards more proactive community care. I then held the role of quality improvement lead for SLaM for 2 years and was the lead for CAMHS improvement up to 2017. I think joined NHS England as was part of the team that developed Lord Carters review into community and mental health services. During the COVID 19 pandemic I was part of the national incident coordination centre in NHS England and for the 18 months after the pandemic, I was deployed as the senior programme manager for MSK recovery of services, from orthopaedic services and surgery in hospitals to MSK care in the community and primary care before taking up my current role focusing on personalised care and community services. I have a particular interest in high quality care and improvement and have led on outcomes development in psychosis locally and MSK services nationally over the years. I am also an Institute for Healthcare Improvement (IHI) trained improvement advisor having completed 18 months training in Belfast. In every role, I have been a champion of equality, diversity and inclusion in all roles, particularly race equity and alongside thriving to reduce health inequities, I have supported efforts to focus on the wider determinants of health and better holistic care and support and what matters to people. My hobbies include a real passion for all sports – both watching and playing and in particular, playing basketball, where I have been organising weekly sessions open to all young people but mainly in lewisham and southwark for nearly 15 years where I am also a member of the ladywell hilly fields basketball group, riding my motorcycle on weekend. I also have carer responsibilities for my grandmother.
Alison Coutts R.G.N.; P.C.C.E.A.; PhD
I grew up in Hampshire but came to London to train as a nurse and moved to south-east London shortly after. I have lived here ever since, marrying, and bringing up three children, all now have grown up and left the family home. We keep in touch with each other and often holiday together, in the United Kingdom and Europe. I worship at St Mildred’s Church, Lee and fulfil a number of roles there.
I pursued my nursing career, working in nurse education and currently work at City, University of London. I teach biology to nurses and other health professionals and have a particular interest in career development. I enjoy working in the buzzy environment with students of different backgrounds but all intent on learning to provide the best possible care and to build a career for themselves.
Michelle Fenniche - Chair of Governors
I am an Executive Headteacher within Lewisham Local Authority and have been since September 2016. As I work within two local Primary Schools in the Local Authority and see the great work that is also carried out in our local SEND Schools, I felt that I should be involved in the fantastic work that is being achieved.
I have worked in a number of Local Authorities and enjoyed seeing and being part of the different ways of working. Lewisham is an exciting place for learning and I feel that I am able to support the strategic direction of New Woodlands School, to ensure that the children achieve the best possible outcomes for them as individuals.
I have had a variety of roles over the years, from teacher through to Headteacher and now Executive Headteacher. All of which I have thoroughly enjoyed, seeing so many of our young people of today, achieve their dreams is extremely rewarding.
I am married with 3 wonderful children/adults of my own and am now lucky to have grandchildren to enjoy as well. In my spare time, I spend time with my family and our dogs.
Lisa Hutton - Staff Governor
I have been teaching for 17 years and have a passion for ensuring that every child receives the support and challenge they require to achieve.
After completing a Mathematics degree I have worked in Inner London comprehensive schools with the past 10 years in Lewisham. I currently teach and coordinate Mathematics at New Woodlands School and am the staff representative on the governing board.
As a governor I enjoy supporting the school in moving forward on its journey to provide every child the best opportunity possible.
I moved to the United Kingdom in 2022 and have since made Lewisham my home. My professional journey has spanned several industries, including oil and gas, technology, and now finance, where my current role involves working in the world of cross-border payments.
Joining the Governing Board at New Woodlands School provides an opportunity to contribute to positive change within the community I now call home. With a background in computer science education, I am passionate about applying my analytical and problem-solving skills to support the school’s strategic development and educational mission.
Outside of work, I enjoy engaging with community projects, reading and exploring ways to make a meaningful impact, even in small ways, that help shape opportunities for future generations in Lewisham.
Hello, my Name is Natalie. I have been a Parent Governor for New Woodlands for many years now. My son attended the school for 5 years and left school with 4 GCSEs 5 BTECs and is now at college studying catering. He also ran for young mayor of Lewisham and sits in something called champions of inclusion. He also volunteers as a mentor in our local youth club. This wouldn't of been possible had it not been for the dedicated staff at New Woodlands
Safeguarding and inclusion are my passion. I work alongside families with SEND children and young people, when communication breaks down between parents/carers and professionals I step in and professionally advocate for them to help the child/young person's voice be heard and listened to. This benefits all my families I work with and helps them to see what help is available to them moving forward whether it's EHCP provision, tribunals ect I help. I also am Designated Safeguarding Lead in Judo and Sports.
Happy to talk to anyone who needs to talk .
I have over 40 years experience and knowledge as an educator.
I am retired teacher and headteacher of a special school.
I am a parent , grandmother and now carer for my grandson.
I have continually updated my training and I am willing to continue to advocate for all students, parents and educators of children with Special Educational Needs, especially at New Woodlands school
Having lived in Lewisham since childhood, I attended both primary and secondary school locally, which has given me a strong connection to the area and its community. I later studied Business and Finance at the University of Greenwich, before beginning my career in retail banking, where I worked for eight years. I have since transitioned into a role within the local authority finance department, continuing to build on my financial expertise in a public sector setting.
Joining the Governing Board at New Woodlands School offers me a meaningful opportunity to give back to the community that has shaped me. With my background in finance, I am keen to apply my skills and experience to support the school’s strategic planning and ensure its continued growth and success.
I am a lawyer working in the City and have built my career advising businesses on a range of corporate and commercial matters. Living in Greenwich, I am passionate about supporting the local community and helping young people to achieve their full potential.
I wanted to become a governor because I believe schools play such an important role in shaping confidence, opportunity and future success for children and young people. I am pleased to be able to support New Woodlands School and contribute to the valuable work being carried out by staff and governors alike.
Through my professional experience, I hope to support the strategic direction of the school and help ensure that all pupils are given the best possible opportunities to thrive and succeed as individuals.
Outside of work, I can be found spending time with my family, watching Everton FC and preparing discussion topics for my next book club meeting.

Curriculum Intent
At New Woodlands we aim for every child to be engaged and excited by learning, to become an effective learner and to begin to understand how they learn best. We believe in the concept of lifelong learning and the notion that learning should be a rewarding and enjoyable experience for everyone; it should be fun. Through our teaching we equip children with the skills, knowledge and understanding necessary to be able to make informed choices about the important things in their lives. We believe that appropriate teaching and learning experiences help children to lead happy and rewarding lives. Our learning and teaching policy is at the heart of all we do. It sets out clear expectations, provides a standard uniform approach, a minimum entitlement for every pupil and can be easily monitored ensuring equal opportunity for all our pupils.
